info.title: swipewalk - accessibility scanner for Android and iOS apps (Windows planned
info.description: Accessibility scanner for running Android and iOS apps. Maps automated findings to WCAG 2.2 and writes JSON and HTML reports. Automated checks find only some issues; manual testing is still required.

commands.name: compare
commands.description: What changed between two runs (run folders

options.name: --platform
options.description: Platform of the running app (Windows is not implemented yet)

options.name: --bundle-id
options.description: iOS: bundle identifier of the app to scan

options.name: --device
options.description:
Android: adb serial. iOS: simulator or device UDID (default: the only connected Android
device / the booted simulator). See: swipewalk devices

options.name: --keep-status-bar
options.description:
Android: keep the status bar in screenshots (it is blanked by default to keep
notifications and other personal information out of reports)

options.name: --profile
options.description:
iOS physical devices: installed provisioning profile to sign the harness with (by
default a fitting installed development profile is used, else Xcode automatic signing)

options.name: --harness-bundle-prefix
options.description: iOS: harness bundle id prefix, to fit a company wildcard profile (com.company.*)

options.name: --install
options.description:
Install an already-built app first: Android .apk; iOS Simulator .app (or .zip); iOS
device .ipa signed for the device. The app is never rebuilt or re-signed

options.name: --package
options.description: Android: app package; the pre-flight check confirms it is installed and in front

options.name: --skip-checks
options.description: Skip the pre-flight checks that run before scan and record

options.name: --team
options.description:
iOS physical devices: Apple developer team that signs the scanning harness (found
automatically when there is one; a given team is remembered)

options.name: --harness
options.description: iOS: path to SwipewalkHarness.xcodeproj (default: found from the repo)

options.name: --screen
options.description: Name for the scanned screen in the report (default: "Screen 1")

options.name: --out
options.description: Output directory (default: ./swipewalk-report); runs are also saved to the history

options.name: --no-history
options.description: Don't save this run to the history

options.name: --history
options.description:
History folder to save to (default: the user's Swipewalk/runs folder). Given
explicitly, runs re-scanned with --from are saved too

options.name: --from
options.description: Re-scan a saved capture directory instead of a live device

options.name: --framework
options.description:
App framework for fix examples (Android, and iOS on the Simulator, detect MAUI
automatically, and on an iPhone when installed with --install; overrides detection)

options.name: --large-text
options.description:
scan: also capture at a large system text size (Android 200%; iOS AX3, about 235%,
set through the Settings app on a physical iPhone). On a physical device this
changes the phone's text size and restores it; use a test device. record does
this by default

options.name: --standard
options.description: Focus the report on one standard: ada-title-ii, section-508, en-301-549, en-301-549-v4, uk-public-sector

options.name: --expect
options.description:
record: comma-separated screens you meant to cover; missing ones are listed
scan checks the screen currently shown (bringing the app forward, or starting it, first if needed).
record watches while you use the app and scans each new
screen (Enter: scan now, q: finish). run does what swipewalk.json describes and exits with 3 when
failOn is "wcag-issues" and issues were found. Output: results.json and report.html.
Automated checks find only some issues; manual testing is still required.
